root_causes.root_cause: PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO threshold (0.20) is too tight to absorb Docling extraction non-determinism. RFC-023 D10 widened the threshold from 0.17 to 0.20 but only scoped Doc 5 as the beneficiary. Doc 8 (Reitlehrer, 10 nodes, tree, depth 2) has max_leaf_ratio that jitters between runs (~0.17 in Run 6 vs 0.2571 in Run 7) due to Docling's non-deterministic heading selection/text allocation. The hard threshold comparison at helpers.py:1233 (`max_leaf_ratio < _pass_max_leaf`) flips the verdict from PASS to MARGINAL when jitter pushes the ratio above 0.20. There is no hysteresis, tolerance band, or prior-verdict anchoring to prevent boundary-case oscillation.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two options (choose one): (A) Widen PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO default from 0.20 to 0.30 -- absorbs Doc 8's observed jitter (0.2571) with margin, low risk since max_leaf_ratio > 0.75 is already a hard FAIL gate. (B) Add a tolerance band / hysteresis mechanism: if max_leaf_ratio is within a configurable epsilon (e.g., 0.10) of the threshold AND node_count is small (<=15) AND depth >= 2, still grant PASS. Option A is simpler and consistent with the D10 precedent of threshold widening. The env var PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO already exists for tuning.

root_causes.root_cause: Docling's layout model classifies the primary text-layer content of chart/infographic PDFs as PictureItems, exporting '<!-- image -->' markers instead of actual text. The per-picture OCR recovery pipeline (_recover_picture_text) attempts Tesseract OCR on rendered crops, but this consistently fails for chart-type content: (a) Tesseract produces empty/poor results on vector-art chart labels, and (b) the existing 'clip_text' check at line 1542 reads text-layer content via page.get_text('text', clip=rect) but uses it only to SKIP the region (assuming Docling already extracted the text), never to CAPTURE the text into the PictureResult. There is no fallback path that reads the PDF text layer directly when Docling misclassifies text as images and OCR fails. The raw text layer is present (842-843 chars visible via pypdfium2.get_textpage()) but is never surfaced to the markdown output.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py :: pdf_to_markdown_docling -> _recover_picture_results -> _recover_picture_text (line 1540-1544 clip_text skip, line 1574-1585 OCR)
root_causes.suggested_fix: When _recover_picture_text encounters a region where (a) clip_text has meaningful content (>_PICTURE_OCR_MIN_CHARS) AND (b) the region's text is NOT already in the exported markdown body (i.e., this IS a PictureItem, not a TextItem), capture page.get_text('text', clip=rect) into PictureResult.ocr_text instead of skipping with reason='clip_text'. This reuses the existing text-layer read at line 1542 but routes the text into the recovery result instead of discarding it. Additionally, add a document-level fallback: when Docling produces mostly <!-- image --> markers and very little text (<100 chars excluding markers), read the full page text layer via pypdfium2 and use it as supplementary content.

root_causes.root_cause: The _recover_picture_text Phase 1 crop loop (lines 1518-1566) has no per-region try/except around page.get_pixmap(clip=rect, dpi=300). When PyMuPDF raises 'Invalid bandwriter header dimensions/setup' for ANY single region (confirmed on UAE numbers landscape), the exception propagates up to _recover_picture_results' outer try/except (line 1766), which catches it and returns an empty list []. This causes ALL picture results for the entire document to be lost, even though other regions might have cropped and OCR'd successfully. For doc 14 (UAE landscape), this crash is the direct proximate cause of total content loss: 7 picture regions exist, but the crash on one degenerate region kills recovery for all 7.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py :: _recover_picture_text (lines 1518-1566, Phase 1 crop loop) -> _recover_picture_results (line 1766 outer except)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Wrap the per-region body inside the Phase 1 loop (lines 1518-1566) in a try/except that catches Exception per region, logs a warning, and continues to the next region. On failure, record skip_reasons[i] = 'crop_error' so the ordinal stays dense. This matches the existing dense-list contract documented in _recover_picture_results' docstring ('sparse recovery must never shift ordinals'). The outer except at line 1766 remains as a last-resort guard.

needs_doc_drilldown.reason: Docling extracts 17,734 chars of real content (including tables with row_records) from this 3-page PDF, but the final stored output is only 381 chars in 15 nodes. The converter-level output is adequate; the content loss occurs DOWNSTREAM in the flat extraction pipeline (route_and_extract_flat or the tree->flat fallback path). This diverges from the UAE docs where the converter itself produces near-zero text. Need to trace what happens between Docling's 17,734-char markdown and the 381-char stored result -- likely in how the tree fails depth validation (both headings are H1) and how the flat path measures/stores content from table-heavy blocks.

root_causes.root_cause: split_oversized_leaf_nodes only fires for leaves exceeding 50000 chars OR containing _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE markers (Article/Section/مادة/§/Schedule). After OCR recovery, docs 7 and 21 have lopsided trees where the largest leaf is well under 50k (doc 7: ~7.3k, doc 21: ~15.2k) and does not contain ordinal markers matching the regex. The _has_heading_markers D5a check widens eligibility but only for the same ordinal patterns. Meanwhile, the vendored extract_nodes_from_markdown (page_index_md.py line 33) only builds tree nodes from ATX headings (^#{1,6}\s+), so OCR-recovered text that lacks ATX markdown headings gets lumped under whichever heading the tree builder last saw, concentrating content in a few leaves. The splitter post-pass cannot redistribute because the resulting leaf sizes are below its threshold and the content lacks its recognized marker patterns. This produces leaf_concentration values (0.50 for doc 7, 0.37 for doc 21) well above the PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO threshold of 0.20, locking both at MARGINAL.
root_causes.code_path: client.py:_run_md_to_tree -> page_index_md.extract_nodes_from_markdown (ATX-only heading detection) -> client.py:805 split_oversized_leaf_nodes (50k/ordinal-only trigger) -> helpers.py:1730 eligibility gate
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a secondary splitting strategy in split_oversized_leaf_nodes for leaves that are under 50k but cause leaf_concentration > 0.20 in the overall tree. Options: (1) Add a leaf_concentration-aware pass that splits on paragraph boundaries (blank-line separated blocks) when the tree's max_leaf_ratio exceeds a threshold (e.g., 0.25) even if the leaf is under max_chars; (2) Extend _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE to recognize additional heading patterns common in MOU/decree documents (e.g., 'Clause', 'Part', Arabic بند/باب); (3) Add a post-tree-build rebalancing step that detects lopsided leaf allocation and redistributes text by splitting on blank-line-delimited paragraphs. Option 2 is lowest risk and most targeted.

needs_doc_drilldown.reason: This document has a fundamentally different symptom from docs 7 and 21. It is flat_mixed with depth=1, only 333 chars, and 20 nodes — nearly all content is in image markers with no extractable text. The vendored extract_nodes_from_markdown finds no ATX headings because the source markdown has none (German insurance tariff rendered as images). RFC-023 explicitly marked this out of scope. The issue is content loss at the extraction/converter layer (images not enriched), not a splitter deficiency. Needs separate investigation into why the Docling/converter output for this PDF contains almost no text — likely the PDF is image-only (scanned tariff table) and the OCR/image enrichment pipeline is not recovering its content.

While RC-1 explains WHY the splitter does not fire, confirming it requires inspecting the actual MinIO processed/*.json tree to see which specific leaf holds 50% of the content and what heading patterns exist in the OCR-recovered markdown. The MOU likely uses 'Clause' or similar markers not in _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE. A simple drilldown reading the stored tree JSON would confirm whether extending the regex to include MOU-specific markers (Clause/Part/بند) would resolve this specific document.

RC-1 is the likely shared cause, but this doc already uses Arabic مادة markers that ARE in the regex. The leaf_concentration=0.37 despite 82 nodes and depth=3 suggests the splitter may be firing partially but not fully redistributing content — possibly because some sections use a different Arabic heading pattern (e.g., بند or فقرة sub-articles) that is not in the ordinal regex, or the longest-increasing-run guard is filtering out valid split points. Needs inspection of the stored tree to identify which leaf(s) concentrate the text and what markers they contain.

root_causes.root_cause: D7's `tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages` and the VLM fallback's `vlm_extract_markdown` both depend on the same `rasterize_pdf_pages` function (pypdfium2 at converters.py:2261-2284). When CMap corruption in the source PDF causes pypdfium2 page rendering to fail, both the VLM path (client.py:877 -> converters.py:2321) and the D7 Tesseract fallback path (client.py:916 -> converters.py:2294) crash at the identical `rasterize_pdf_pages` call. D7 was designed as an LLM-free local alternative (RFC-023 D7 spec says 'reuse rasterized page images'), but the implementation calls `tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages(file_path, tess_langs)` which re-rasterizes from scratch using the same pypdfium2 backend, creating a shared single point of failure. The RFC-023 D7 test suite (test_rfc023_d7.py) only tests the reason-override logic in isolation, never exercising the actual rasterization path, so this SPOF was not caught. The preprocess.log confirms doc 18 ('القرار التنظيمي') consistently errors with exit code 1.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:909-916 -> src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:2287-2307 -> src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:2261-2284 (rasterize_pdf_pages, shared with vlm_extract_markdown at converters.py:2310-2321)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Give `tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages` an alternative rasterization backend that does not share the pypdfium2 SPOF. PyMuPDF's `fitz.Page.get_pixmap()` is already imported and used in the codebase for image cropping (`_recover_picture_text` in converters.py). Add a `rasterize_pdf_pages_fitz(pdf_path, dpi)` function that uses fitz, and modify `tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages` to try pypdfium2 first, then fall back to fitz on failure. This isolates the D7 rasterization from the VLM rasterization, so a CMap-corrupted PDF that crashes pypdfium2 can still be rasterized via fitz for Tesseract OCR. Note: fitz is AGPL (PyMuPDF) but is already a transitive dependency -- the AGPL concern (Hard Rule 4) is already accepted for the existing fitz usage in the pre-garble probe (client.py:597-611) and picture cropping.

root_causes.root_cause: D7's Tesseract-on-raster fallback is structurally nested inside the VLM `except Exception as vlm_exc:` block (client.py:894-937). It is only reachable when `vlm_extract_markdown` or the subsequent `_run_md_to_tree` raises an exception. If the VLM succeeds at extracting markdown from the rasterized pages but the rendered text is garbled (CMap corruption causes wrong glyph rendering), and the LLM tree generation also succeeds (producing a tree from garbled VLM text), then `validate_tree` at line 890-892 returns `(False, 'garbling')` and the `try` block completes normally -- the `except` block (and D7) is never entered. The code falls through to `LowQualityTreeError('garbling')`. This is by design (RFC-023 D7 test case (d): 'garbling reason without VLM exception -- existing escalation path unchanged'), but it means D7 cannot recover documents where the VLM 'succeeds' but produces unusable garbled output. The preprocess.log stderr_tail shows litellm completion calls (gpt-4.1 via Azure), consistent with a tree generation LLM call succeeding rather than the VLM crashing.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:867-893 (try block where VLM succeeds) vs src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:894-937 (except block where D7 lives)
root_causes.suggested_fix: After the VLM's `validate_tree` at line 890-893, when `ok` is still False and reason is 'garbling' (VLM succeeded but tree is still garbled), add the same D7 Tesseract-on-raster recovery logic INSIDE the `try` block, not only in the `except` block. This covers the case where VLM 'succeeds' but produces garbled output. The existing `except`-block D7 continues to handle VLM crashes. Extract the D7 logic into a helper function to avoid duplication.
